description: Standard persona-specific Figma email prompt rules (dark mode).
rules: Standard persona requirement: build the email starting from the exact boilerplate of the approved master template reference (references/master_template.html): the XHTML 1.0 Transitional doctype, html namespaces (xmlns:v, xmlns:o), the MSO gte-9 OfficeDocumentSettings conditional block, all meta tags including format-detection, the complete CSS reset and email-client fixes (.ExternalClass, .em_defaultlink, .em_g_img + div, a[x-apple-data-detectors]), the full responsive utility class library, the 599px/480px/374px breakpoints, and the em_full_wrap/em_main_table wrapper structure with body class em_body. Set the document title and main-table width from the Figma metadata. The sample content blocks inside the reference remain forbidden as content sources; where a master-template breakpoint forces a fixed 375px or 320px mobile main-table width, the Standard fluid-width rule below overrides it and mobile em_main_table must stay width:100% !important.
Standard persona requirement: copy the complete approved stylesheet, including color-scheme declarations and the approved prefers-color-scheme dark media query.

Standard persona requirement: include both dark-mode meta tags before the style block and keep every mobile em_main_table rule fluid with width:100% !important; never force 375px or 320px mobile main-table widths.
Figma colors describe normal/light mode only. Apply only the approved Standard dark-mode classes to qualifying backgrounds, text, links, and CTAs.

Standard dark-mode class mapping: light/white surfaces use em_darkbg; dark/black text uses em_dm_txt_white; white/light text uses em_dm_txt_black when it must stay readable after Standard inversion; dark surfaces that must invert to light use em_lightbg.

Apply the Standard mapping directly to colored links, CTA anchors, and CTA button cells when those elements have their own inline color or background; do not rely only on a parent class for directly colored CTA/link text.

Apply Standard dark mode from installed Standard package rules/references only; do not search local folders, sibling files, old outputs, or local examples to discover dark-mode patterns unless the user explicitly permits it.
